workLog.phase: Merge main and re-bump the plugin manifests
actions: Opened pull request 3442. GitHub reported CONFLICTING while a local merge-tree of the same two commits reported clean, so only 12 checks ran instead of the usual full suite: GitHub could not build the merge ref

Diagnosed the cause rather than force-pushing blind. The generated causal graph under .agents/memory/causality/ is declared with a custom merge driver in .gitattributes. That driver is configured on this machine and is not available to GitHub server side, so a file both branches touch resolves locally and conflicts remotely
Merged origin/main into the branch locally, where the driver runs, instead of rebasing. A rebase would have required a force push, which the universal rules prohibit on a shared branch

Main had itself shipped plugin version 0.6.129 while this branch was in review, so the branch bump was no longer strictly greater than base. Bumped both manifests to 0.6.130 to satisfy the parity gate

Re-checked every issue this change cites. Issue 3424, filed during the first phase, was closed as completed by pull request 3432 on main. Confirmed no document on this branch still claims it is open: the only two mentions are the generated causal graph and this dated session log
workLog.outcome: Branch contains the tip of main, the causal graph is resolved by the driver that owns it, and both plugin manifests are strictly greater than base at 0.6.130.
